stories.title: Bus crash on Egypt's Red Sea coast kills 16
stories.summary: At least 16 people have been killed in a bus crash in eastern Egypt, the country's health ministry has said. Another 28 people were injured on the road between Red Sea towns of Dahab and Nuweiba in the South Sinai governorate on Wednesday morning. As many as 20 ambulances were sent to the scene of the accident to provide first aid and evacuate the injured, the ministry said. The cause of the crash remains unknown. The area is a popular tourist destination, attracting visitors from around the world.

stories.title: Baby found alive in sanitary bin at Penang airport toilet
stories.summary: The police have reportedly detained a man and a woman believed to be linked to the case.
article_sentences: A newborn is believed to have been found alive inside a sanitary bin at a toilet at the Penang International Airport in Malaysia on Sept 1.
According to news reports, the baby was said to have been delivered shortly before it was discovered, with the placenta and umbilical cord still attached.
The shocking discovery was captured in three videos that have since gone viral on social media.

stories.summary: Study of language has been close to us since the ancient Indian grammarian Panini worked out to scientifically understand Sankrit across time and tradition. Today, linguistics boomerangs between not just tradition and time, but modern concerns of technology and cognition.

stories.summary: Israeli army says earlier interception likely 'false target' The Israeli military said that its interception of a "suspicious aerial target" was "apparently launched at a false target". Earlier, the army announced that "interceptors were launched toward a suspicious aerial target," alleging that it crossed from Lebanese territory into northern Israel.

stories.title: Tyson Fury confirms Anthony Joshua fight at NYC’s Madison Square Garden
stories.summary: No date has been set for the all-British heavyweight boxing showdown but it is expected to be held in November. Former world heavyweight champion. Tyson Fury has confirmed that his long-awaited heavyweight boxing showdown with fellow Briton Anthony Joshua will take place at New York City’s iconic Madison Square Garden. No exact date has been set for the Joshua vs Fury fight — one of the biggest in British boxing history — although it is expected to be held in November after both signed a contract with Turki Alalshikh, Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority chairman. “What a place, what a venue, what a fight,” Fury said in a post on Instagram. Fury called New York City “the land of opportunity”, but fans criticised him in comments on the post as they questioned why an all-British fight was being held in the US, and not at a location like Wembley Stadium in the United Kingdom. Fury, who turned 38 in August, has won 36 professional bouts, suffering his only losses in two fights with Ukraine’s Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. He announced his return to boxing in January, having retired from the sport in December 2024 after losing to Usyk in a bout for three of the four major world titles. Joshua and Fury were unable to agree on terms in 2021, and plans for the face-off fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead. In the lead-up to the Joshua showdown, Fury forced Polish opponent Mariusz Wach to retire in a tune-up bout in July attended by some 1,500 fans at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya, Thailand.

stories.title: Australia, US commit $739 million to support Pacific Island nations
stories.summary: This includes a $545 million package from Australia to combat drug smuggling in the region.
article_sentences: Australia and the US have pledged a total of US$580 million to support Pacific Island nations amid growing Chinese influence in the region.
US funding focuses on energy security and grid stability, while Australia targets drug smuggling with enhanced surveillance and training.
The 2026 Pacific Islands Forum is marked by tensions over Taiwan's participation.
SYDNEY/WASHINGTON – Australia and the United States on Sept 2 announced a combined US$580 million (S$739 million) in funding for the Pacific Islands as they battle China for influence in the region.

The US contribution, while smaller at US$150 million, is one of the most public signals from the Trump administration that it is still engaged in the Pacific after it dismantled the US Agency for International Development in 2025.

The funding, announced by Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau at the 2026 meeting of the Pacific Islands Forum in Palau, follows an increase in China’s influence in recent years via grants, infrastructure projects and donations.

These include the donation of a presidential building complex in Vanuatu, a comprehensive strategic partnership with the Solomon Islands including a deal on policing cooperation as well as a comprehensive strategic partnership with the Cook Islands.

“Chinese measures in the region are a forcing function for the US to understand to be more deliberate in their engagement,” said Jared Mondschein, director of research at the United States Studies Centre.
The US funding includes US$60 million to help countries address the global energy crisis by expanding fuel storage capacity and supporting grid stability.
The region has been badly hurt by the Iran war exacerbating energy security concerns, said Oliver Nobetau, the Lowy Institute’s Pacific Islands Program director.
The fallout has resulted in “slowing economies, prioritisation of essential services, all against the backdrop of a super El Nino – which require support from external partners to curb,” he added.
Australia said it will offer.
